name: Museumsfriedhof Kramsach
kurzbeschreibung: The Museumsfriedhof Kramsach ('Lustiger Friedhof'): a unique open-air museum featuring whimsical, humorous epitaphs and five centuries of wrought-iron craftsmanship.
beschreibung:
Overview

The world-famous Museumsfriedhof Kramsach – colloquially known as the 'Lustiger Friedhof' ('Cheerful Cemetery') or 'Cemetery without Dead' – is located in the tranquil hamlet of Hagau in the Tyrolean municipality of Kramsach in the district of Kufstein. This unique open-air museum ranks among the most visited and original cultural-historical attractions in western Austria. Set on an idyllic meadow shaded by mature trees, over 900 artfully forged historic wrought-iron grave crosses and burial plaques from across the Alpine region are gathered. They bear witness to an archaic, deeply rooted folk culture that confronted death not with dread, but with life-affirming, subtle, and occasionally earthy humor.

History & Roguish Epitaphs

The open-air museum was founded in 1965 on the initiative of Kramsach master blacksmith and stonemason Hans Guggenberger. Guggenberger recognized the invaluable cultural and historical value of the antique hand-forged grave crosses, which were ending up by the thousands in scrap heaps during cemetery clearances across Bavaria, Tyrol, and the Salzburg region. With great passion, he collected, derusted, and restored these wrought-iron works of art spanning five centuries (from the 17th to the early 20th century). Not a single person is buried beneath these graves – the meadow serves solely as an exhibition area. The museum's enduring appeal lies in the candid, profound, and roguish epitaphs that humorously capture the lives, mishaps, and frailties of the deceased without pretension. Famous rhyming verses include: 'Hier liegt die Jungfrau Rosalia Bopp, sie starb an einem Bienenstopp, die Biene stach ihr in die Zung, da war’s vorbei mit der Hoffnung' ('Here lies the virgin Rosalia Bopp, who died of a bee-stop: the bee stung her tongue, and hope was forever undone') or 'Hier liegt Martin Krug, der Zähne, Weib und Kinder trug. Zeig Himmel, ihm ein leiseres Asyl, als ihm das Erdenleben bot!' ('Here lies Martin Krug, who bore teeth, wife, and child. Grant him, Heaven, a quieter refuge than earthly life offered!'). A dedicated covered arcade and a small museum shop complete the ensemble.

Visit & Getting There

The Museumsfriedhof Kramsach is open to visitors daily year-round from 09:00 to 18:00 (until 19:00 in summer). Admission to the open-air museum is free (voluntary donations at the entrance for the preservation and ongoing maintenance of the precious ironwork are appreciated). Arriving by car: Via the Inntalautobahn A12, exit Kramsach/Alpbachtal, continue towards Kramsach center and follow the signs for 'Museumsfriedhof / Hagau' (a large free parking lot is available directly at the Hagau 2 entrance). By public transport: Train (ÖBB) to Brixlegg station, from where VVT bus line 4111 or 4074 runs every half hour directly to the Kramsach Museumsfriedhof stop.

Tips

The entire museum grounds are level with well-maintained gravel and grass paths, making them fully accessible for wheelchair users and strollers. Take your time strolling among the crosses to read the often finely scripted rhymes in peace and admire the intricate wrought-iron embellishments. In the adjacent museum cafe and shop, visitors can purchase books compiling the collected epitaphs as a delightful Tyrolean souvenir.
oeffnungszeiten: Ganzjährig täglich von 09:00 bis 18:00 Uhr (im Sommer bis 19:00 Uhr) geöffnet
